technology_name: Nature-Inspired Neurotoxins from Nepenthes: Insecticidal and Therapeutic Compounds
institution: KSCSTE- Jawaharlal Nehru Tropical Botanic Garden & Research Institute (JNTBGRI)
problem_solved: Need for natural, plant-based acetylcholinesterase (AChE) inhibitors for safe agricultural pest control and Alzheimer's disease therapeutics.
description: Indian Nepenthes pitcher plants act as natural CO₂ chambers, secreting an extrafloral nectar (EFN) laced with (+)-isoshinanolone, a natural inhibitor of acetylcholinesterase (AChE). This neurotoxic compound acts as a 'toxic sugar bait' that impairs neuronal activity and flight response in insects. This discovery reveals the plant's deceptive prey capture strategy and identifies a potent dual-use molecule. The extracted AChE inhibitor presents strong translational potential as both a safe, natural insecticide for agriculture and a promising candidate molecule for Alzheimer's disease therapy, blending ecology with pharmacology.
applications:
• Commercial development of natural, bio-based insecticides for agricultural pest management

• Pharmaceutical research and drug development for Alzheimer's disease therapies

• Biomimicry and chemical synthesis of (+)-isoshinanolone for commercial applications

• Biodiversity conservation and chemical profiling of endemic carnivorous plants
